replication.target_description: Kontkanen (2024), section 4.2.1 and Table 4 current-study article column: chi-square comparison of article TLU rates between beginners (A1+A2) and intermediates (B1+B2). Matching is based on the named morpheme and comparison, not numeric values.

n.sample_role: Unresolved analytic count of morpheme contexts/annotations for the chi-square test; not the contributor count of 40 learner texts.
n.exclusions: 127 eligible contributors were narrowed to 40 texts on word count; all four proficiency groups contribute. No critical-test contingency counts or explicit analytic-N/exclusion statement are supplied. Obligatory contexts and non-obligatory oversuppliance annotations are distinguished in the methods.

reported_success.quote:
Although the results of the current study suggest that, contrary to the reference study, there
are no major differences in accuracy orders between beginner and intermediate learners, the
factors of age and number of years studying English should be considered.

notes: Only n_r and reported_success were assigned; original, replication es and replication p are unassigned null placeholders. Figure 4 explicitly labels 572 as the total number of article annotations. This is retained as a candidate, not certified as Table 4 analytic N. The study distinguishes OC from NOC/oversuppliance (pp.19–20), defines TLU rate as SOC/OC (p.24), and uses the group score method across all learners (pp.41–42). Table 4 supplies chi-square and p values without N or underlying contingency cells. Forty texts are contributor units and are not substituted for morpheme-context observations. No N sum or effect-size conversion was performed. The authors describe study-level disagreement with the reference study (p.44), and significance patterns (p.30), but do not label replication success for this particular Table 4 comparison. No per-effect verdict is inferred from matching significance or from conclusions about acquisition ranks or error subtypes. Rendered PDF pp.23 and 31 were inspected for Figure 4 and Table 4 layout.
